claims.text: As-cast high-entropy alloy samples have inhomogeneous grain structures.
As-cast high-entropy alloy samples have relatively high defect densities.
Controlled annealing reduces microstructural inhomogeneity, defect density, and grain-boundary area.
Reducing defect density and grain-boundary area produces more uniform magnetic domains and exchange interactions.
Microstructural homogenization and lower residual stress produce more uniform magnetic-domain alignment.
Microstructural homogenization enhances coupling between lattice and magnetic degrees of freedom.
More uniform magnetic exchange interactions enhance the magnetocaloric response at low applied fields.
Annealed samples will show a greater low-field magnetic entropy change or adiabatic temperature change than untreated samples.
Annealed samples will exhibit lower magnetic hysteresis than untreated samples.
Annealing will minimally affect thermal conductivity and will preserve rapid heat exchange.
Annealing will preserve mechanical integrity or stability.
Untreated samples have lower magnetocaloric efficiency and higher hysteresis because of microstructural inhomogeneity.
The proposed behavior should hold under alloy-specific moderate annealing conditions.
Extreme annealing temperatures or durations may cause adverse phase changes or microstructural coarsening.
The comparison will be conducted below approximately 1 T and near room temperature.
An untreated control and a controlled-annealing treatment group will be compared using microstructural, magnetic, calorimetric, thermal, and mechanical measurements.
